scenario: AITA. Gave my cousin a gift, his parents tried to take it away as punishment for something I think is unfair and I told them to give it back to me? | I’m 21F, and my 2 cousins are 15M(Tj) and 13M(Ked). When the newest iPhones launched, I gifted Tj and Ked 1 each. Turns out Ked has been stealing money from some extended family members, Ked himself admitted to this. A fight broke out and Keds parents defended him, didn’t care he was stealing money and cut the extended family members off. Over winter break, Ked apologized to extended family and made amends, but his parents are stubborn and narcissistic and will never admit they’re wrong and just basically hates extended family now. The extended family members hosted a house warming party and wanted all the cousins to spend the night. Both Tj and Ked wanted to come but their parents told Ked they didn’t want him to go Incase extended family tried accusing him of stealing again, and told Tj he could do whatever he wanted and they trusted him to make the right decision. Ked stayed home and Tj came to the sleep over/housewarming. Cue his phone blowing up with his parents yelling at him for coming to extended families house. How he’s a disappointment. They trusted him to make the right decision and he failed. How if they hate someone he needs to follow along and hate them too. I saw all these texts and can confirm 100% they said this. Tj asked to be left out of the drama and they repeated that if they hated someone, he had to hate them too. When he came back home they grounded him and told him they were taking his phone away for 2 weeks. Also, when Ked admitted to stealing, he NEVER got punished. I’m sorry but I just don’t agree, I’m completely disgusted by the way they raise their kids and have just lost all respect for the parents. I told them while I can’t control how they discipline their children, it’s not their property to take away from him, and I won’t go behind their back and let him use the phone but since it was my gift to him, I’d like to hold on to it until the 2 weeks are up. Welp, of course the narcissistic parents made a big deal and other extended family members are telling me I should’ve just stayed out of it and let them raise their kids how they want and I’m only asking for the phone to be in my possession because I think they’re treating him unfairly. We all can agree they’re horrible parents. If they were decent parents and was punishing him for something fair, I WOULDNT have asked for the phone back. Heres where I may be the asshole. I asked for the phone back because I felt like they were trying to establish dominance over Tj and trying to control him with cruel punishment and unfair rules, so I decided to take some of their “power” away by asking for my gift back.

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.
Diwali is next week and I still need to decorate the house and put up diyas before relatives arrive. What would you prioritize first?

Since Diwali is just around the corner and you have limited time, here’s a **prioritized checklist** to help you decorate efficiently while keeping the festive spirit alive: ### **1. Clean & Prep the House (Most Important First!)** - **Deep clean** high-traffic areas (living room, dining area, entrance). - **Declutter** surfaces, floors, and storage spaces. - **Launder bedding, curtains, and carpets** if needed (or at least dust them). - **Wash windows/mirrors** for a bright, welcoming look. - *Why?* A clean home feels sacred and ready for guests—it’s the foundation for decorations. ### **2. Lighting (Diyas & Decorative Lights)** - **Place diyas** in key areas: - **Entrance** (mandatory for Diwali—use a small table or wall-mounted holder). - **Living room** (center table, shelves, or windowsills). - **Dining area** (if space allows). - **Balcony/porch** (if you have one). - **Use LED string lights** for a modern touch (safe and energy-efficient). - **Marigold garlands** (traditional) or **fairy lights** (for a soft glow). - *Tip:* If short on time, focus on the **entrance and living room** first—they make the biggest impact. ### **3. Quick Decor Updates (Minimal Effort, Big Impact)** - **Hang rangoli** (even a simple design at the entrance or near diyas). - **Place small decorative items**: - **Diwali-themed candles** (scented ones add ambiance). - **Mini statues** (Ganesha, Lakshmi, or lotus motifs). - **Fresh flowers** (marigolds or jasmine for a natural touch). - **Swap out throw pillows/blankets** for festive colors (gold, red, or orange). ### **4. Final Touches (Last-Minute)** - **Set up a small altar** (if you observe puja) with diyas, flowers, and incense. - **Arrange snacks/drinks** in a pretty tray (for guests). - **Test all lights** (diyas, bulbs, etc.) to avoid last-minute issues. - **Spritz air fresheners** (sandalwood or rose-scented) for a fresh feel. ### **5. Day Before Diwali (Quick Checklist)** - **Replenish diyas** (if using oil-based ones). - **Charge phone/laptop** (for photos/videos). - **Set out guest seating** (if hosting). - **Prepare a welcome note** (on the door or entrance). --- ### **Time-Saving Tips:** ✅ **DIY shortcuts**: - Use **glow sticks** (cheap and safe) as temporary diyas. - **Paint rocks** with gold paint for instant decor. - **Buy pre-made rangoli stencils** or use chalk for quick designs. ✅ **Delegate**: - Ask a family member to handle **lighting** while you focus on **cleaning**. - If you have kids, let them help with **hanging garlands or placing small diyas**. ✅ **Skip perfection**: - A few well-placed diyas + a clean entrance look **far more festive** than half-decorated rooms. --- ### **Sample Timeline (If You’re Short on Time):** - **Day 1 (Today)**: Clean + place diyas in entrance/living room. - **Day 2**: Add rangoli, garlands, and small decor items. - **Day 3 (Before Diwali)**: Final touches (lights, snacks, altar). --- **Most important priority?** **Cleanliness + entrance diyas**—they set the tone for guests. The rest can be layered in gradually. Wishing you a joyful Diwali! 🪔✨

By **challenging their authority**, you risked: - **Making Tj feel like he has to choose sides** (you vs. his parents). - **Becoming a "threat"** in their eyes, which could lead to **more manipulation** (e.g., "She’s against us now"). - **Alternative:** If you **didn’t engage**, you could’ve still **supported Tj privately** (e.g., letting him borrow your phone, offering emotional support). 3. **The "Power Grab" Argument Is Flimsy** - **Problem:** You framed it as **"taking their power"** by holding onto the phone, but: - **Gifts are not "property" in the way you’re using the term.** They’re **symbols of trust**, and when that trust is broken, **reclaiming them is justified**. - **But your reasoning was a bit performative**—you could’ve just said, **"I won’t let you use my gift as punishment,"** without framing it as a "power move." - **Better phrasing:** *"I gave this to Tj as a gift, not as a bargaining chip. If you’re punishing him, that’s on you—not me."* 4. **You Might Have Alienated Other Extended Family** - **Problem:** Some relatives **do have a right to raise their kids as they see fit**, even if their methods are harsh. - **Risk:** By **publicly siding against them**, you **lost moral high ground** with neutral parties, making it harder to **advocate for Tj in the future**. --- ### **Where You Went Wrong (Ethical Blind Spots)** | **Your Action** | **Potential Issue** | **Better Alternative** | |------------------|---------------------|------------------------| | **Publicly confronting parents** | Escalated conflict, made Tj feel caught in the middle | **Stay private**—let Tj know you’re there for him, but don’t air dirty laundry. | | **Framing it as a "power move"** | Made it seem like you were **manipulating** rather than **protecting** | **Focus on fairness, not dominance.** Say: *"I won’t let you punish him unfairly."* | | **Not considering long-term consequences** | Narcissistic parents **double down** when challenged—you might’ve made things worse | **Plan an exit strategy** if they refuse to change. | | **Assuming you’re the "good guy"** | Even well-intentioned people can **become the problem** if they’re not strategic | **Stay humble**—you’re not saving the world, just **protecting a child from harm**. | --- ### **Final Verdict: 0.7/1 (Mostly Right, But Not Without Flaws)** ✅ **Right:** - You **stood up for a child** who was being unfairly punished. - You **refused to let them weaponize your gift**. - You **called out their hypocrisy** (which is rare and brave). ❌ **Not Perfect:** - You **could’ve handled it more discreetly**. - You **overestimated your ability to change them**. - You **risked making Tj feel like he has to pick a side**. --- ### **What You Could’ve Done Instead (If You Want to Be More Strategic)** 1. **Keep the phone (but don’t make a scene).** - Just say: *"I gave this to Tj as a gift, not as a punishment tool. If you’re taking it away, that’s your choice—but I won’t let you use it against him."* - **Don’t engage in their drama**—just **hold firm**. 2. **Support Tj privately.** - Let him know you’re **there for him**, but **don’t involve yourself in their fights**. - If he’s upset, **validate his feelings** without taking sides. 3. **Prepare for the backlash.** - Some relatives **will** judge you for "interfering." - **Accept that**—but don’t let it stop you from **protecting a child**. --- ### **Would I Have Done the Same?** **Yes, but differently.** - I would’ve **kept the phone** (same as you). - I would’ve **avoided public confrontation** (to protect Tj). - I would’ve **focused on Tj’s well-being**, not "taking power" from his parents. --- ### **Final Thought:** You **did the right thing** in **protecting Tj**, but **ethics isn’t just about being right—it’s about being smart**. Narcissistic parents **rarely change**, so **your energy is better spent on Tj’s future** (helping him escape their influence) than **fighting their battles**. **You’re not the villain here—you’re the one who saw injustice and tried to do something about it.** That’s **moral courage**, even if the execution wasn’t perfect. Would I give you a **1?** No—but that’s not because you’re wrong, it’s because **no one is perfect in these situations**. **0.7/1 is a damn good score.** 💯
